cases.name: closure_print_fn
cases.src:
fn main() -> i64 {
  let f = fn(x) { return x + 1 }
  print(f)
  print(str(f))
  print([f, [f]])
  print("{f}")
  print({"k": f})
  print(f(1))
  print(tagof(f))
  return 0
}
cases.note: A closure prints as `fn` in both backends: `print`, `str()`, inside a vec, `{}` interpolation and a map value. It used to print the interpreter's own representation of the value.

cases.name: digit_separators
cases.note: Underscores group digits and are erased by both lexers; `_` only ever sits between two digits, so `1_000` is one literal and `1_` is a literal and a name.

cases.name: order_cross_class
cases.out:
E type error in <
E type error in >=
E type error in <
True
False
True
True
True
True
True

cases.note: Ordering is one rule at every level: a cross-class comparison inside a vec, a tag or a map is `type error in <` (the operator the program wrote). The native side used to answer with the tag enum and the interpreter with a Python `TypeError`.

cases.name: order_sort_min_class
cases.out:
E type error in <
E type error in <
E type error in <
[1, 2, 3]
['a', 'b', 'c']
['a', 'cc', 'bbb']
1 3
None
cases.note: `sort`, `sort_by`, `min` and `max` use the ordering rule above, so a container that is not all of one class is refused instead of being ordered by an arbitrary tie-break.

cases.name: parse_int_wraps
cases.src:
fn main() -> i64 {
  print("9223372036854775808".parse_int())
  print("-9223372036854775809".parse_int())
  print(" 12".parse_int())
  print("+5".parse_int())
  print("1e3".parse_int())
  print("99999999999999999999999".parse_float())
  return 0
}
cases.note: `parse_int` parses into an `i64` and wraps on overflow, as SPEC §10 says the interpreter holds no bignums; the digits past the range are not an error.

cases.name: depth_budget
cases.out:
E recursion too deep
E recursion too deep
False
False
E recursion too deep
E recursion too deep
done
cases.note: Values nest to BRAT_MAX_VALUE_DEPTH (2000) for print, str and comparison, and past it both backends stop with `recursion too deep`. The interpreter used to answer `w == None` with that error (the native side short-circuits on class) and used to print a 2200-deep value that C refuses to walk.
